about.title: About | The Art World Report
about.description: The Art World Report explains how the art trade works: how galleries price and place work, what auction houses charge, and what the numbers in the headlines mean.

settings.heading: Understanding the *Business* of Art.
settings.text: The Art World Report is about the business side of art: galleries, auction houses, fairs, and the money that moves between them. We write for collectors, artists and anyone else who wants to know how the trade works.

cards.title: Sourced
cards.text: Every fact and figure comes from a published source, and we link to it in the article and list it at the end.

cards.title: Nothing invented
cards.text: We do not make up quotes, interviews, examples or statistics. When we could not find something out, we say so.

cards.title: Prices as reported
cards.text: Auction prices keep their original currency, and we say whether a figure is the hammer price or includes the buyer's premium.

cards.title: Who is behind a figure
cards.text: When a figure comes from someone with an interest in it, such as a consultancy that sells the service it measures, we point that out.

cards.title: Not advice
cards.text: We explain how the market works. We do not tell anyone what to buy or sell.

cards.title: Corrections
cards.text: If we get something wrong, [tell us](contact/). We will check it and put it right.

privacy.title: Privacy | The Art World Report
privacy.description: How The Art World Report handles information about visitors: what is collected, by whom, and why.

settings.body:
This page explains what happens to information about you when you visit The Art World Report. The short version: we do not run analytics, we do not use advertising cookies, and we do not ask you for personal details.

Who we are

The Art World Report is published at theartworldreport.com. You can reach us at info@grovegallery.com.

What the site itself collects

Nothing. The site is a set of plain web pages. It has no accounts, no comments and no tracking code, and it does not set cookies.

The newsletter form on the Briefing page is not connected to any mailing service yet. If you type an email address into it, the address stays in your browser and is not sent anywhere. We will update this page before sign-up opens.

Services the site relies on

Three outside services are involved when a page loads. Each one receives the technical details that any website receives, such as your IP address and browser type.

  • GitHub Pages hosts the site. GitHub may keep server logs for security and to run the service. See the GitHub privacy statement.
  • Google Fonts supplies the typefaces. See the Google Fonts FAQ, which covers privacy.
  • jsDelivr supplies a small script that makes scrolling smoother. See jsDelivr's terms and policies. If it does not load, the site works as normal.

If you email us

We will see your email address and anything you include in the message. We use it only to reply, and we do not add you to any list.

Links to other sites

Our articles link to their sources. Those sites have their own privacy policies, and what happens there is up to them.

Your rights

If you are in the UK or the EU, data protection law gives you rights over personal information held about you, including the right to see it and to have it deleted. As we do not collect anything through the site, in practice this applies only to emails you have sent us. Write to the address above and we will deal with it. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office.

terms.title: Terms | The Art World Report
terms.description: The terms for using The Art World Report: what our articles are for, what they are not, and how you may use them.

settings.body:
By using this site you agree to these terms. They are written to be read, so please do.

What our articles are for

The Art World Report explains how the art trade works. Our articles are general information, not financial, legal, tax or investment advice. Art prices can go down as well as up, and a past auction result does not tell you what a work will fetch in future. Before you buy, sell or donate a work of art, take advice from someone who knows your circumstances.

Accuracy

We take every fact and figure from a published source and link to it. Sources can be wrong or change, and auction houses change their fees from time to time. Each article shows the date it was written. If you find a mistake, please tell us and we will look into it.

Where we report an auction price we say whether it is the hammer price or includes the buyer's premium, and where we have not checked a figure against the auction house's own records we say that too.

Using our content

The text of this site belongs to The Art World Report. You are welcome to quote short passages with a link back to the article. Please ask us before copying whole articles or republishing them elsewhere.

Names of auction houses, galleries, fairs and other businesses belong to their owners. Mentioning them does not mean they endorse or are connected with this site.

Links to other sites

We link to the sources we use. We are not responsible for what other sites publish, and a link is not an endorsement.

Changes

We may update these terms. The date at the top shows when they last changed.

Law

These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.
